findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === never match
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable the zero-length/unavailable override branch does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`. Dayjs instances are objects so === is always false. The intended all-day-blocked override case is therefore dead code and such overrides fall through to the generic inside/outside logic instead of returning unavailable.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects valid slots and accepts days with no hours
findings.body: The added workingHours guard uses `workingHours.find(...)` where the predicate returns true when the slot is outside that single entry. With multiple entries for the same weekday (split hours) one matching entry and one non-matching entry makes find() truthy, so a slot inside valid hours is rejected. Conversely if no workingHours entry contains slotStartTime.day(), find() returns undefined and the slot falls through to the busy check and is treated as available, so days with no working hours become bookable.

findings.title: Date overrides filtered by start only and reduced to time-of-day
findings.body: In getSlots activeOverrides only tests `override.start` against the invitee day range and then converts overrides to `startTime/endTime` minutes from `hour()*60+minute()`, discarding the day. An override that starts on another calendar day in the invitee timezone but spills into this day, or one whose timezone shift pushes it across midnight, is either ignored for this day or wraps to start>end / truncated minutes, producing wrong or no slots for invitee timezones far from the organizer.

findings.title: Override offset uses string parsing inconsistent with time math
findings.body: Offset is computed from `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(...).utcOffset()` while times are computed from `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset)`. toString() renders in server-local format and re-parsing it before applying tz is locale/DST fragile and inconsistent with the second computation, so organizer-to-invitee shift can be off by the server offset or DST difference.
